section_summary: This section concerns Japanese permission requirements for American flights over the South Manchuria Railway Zone and the Kwantung Leased Territory, prompted by Perry Hutton’s Ford Motor Company flight. Embassy correspondence recounts the permissions sought and compares the legal status of the railway zone with that of leased territory. Two enclosed letters discuss earlier foreign flights and U.S. views on jurisdiction in Kwantung.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Consul General Myers’s despatch No. 353
subfiles.from: Mahlon F. Perkins, for the American Minister
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt and forwarding of Myers’s September 20, 1930 despatch.
subfiles.summary: Perkins acknowledges the despatch and says copies were sent to the Department of State and the Embassy at Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Minister Johnson on Japanese flight requirements
subfiles.from: Francis White, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards an instruction to the Ambassador at Tokyo about flights over the South Manchuria Railway Zone.
subfiles.summary: White sends Johnson a copy of the Department’s instruction concerning Japanese requirements raised in the Mukden consul general’s despatch.

subfiles.title: Document file note for despatch No. 103
subfiles.about: Indexes Forbes’s despatch about flight requirements encountered by Perry Hutton.
subfiles.summary: Indexes despatch No. 103 under Ford Motor Company flights over Japanese territory and railway and fortified zones.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 103 on Japanese requirements for airplane flights
subfiles.about: Explains permissions sought for Hutton’s flight and the Embassy’s view of Japanese authority over the railway zone.
subfiles.summary: Forbes recounts Embassy requests and Japanese restrictions on Perry Hutton’s 1930 flight, including the refusal to allow him to land at Dairen and permission to cross the railway zone at Mukden. He disputes evidence that other foreign aviators received more favorable treatment. The despatch argues that prior U.S. treatment of leased territory supports Japanese administrative authority in the railway zone, while leaving the effect of China’s repudiation of the 1915 convention unresolved.

subfiles.title: Embassy letter seeking comment on flights over the railway zone
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, for the Ambassador
subfiles.about: Requests evidence and the Legation’s views on Myers’s account of foreign flights and Japanese authority.
subfiles.summary: Dooman seeks evidence of later flights across the zone without consent and asks the Legation to comment on the zone’s legal status. He also corrects a transmitted phrase in an Embassy telegram.

subfiles.title: Neville letter on jurisdiction in the Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.about: Reviews published U.S. correspondence on sovereignty and consular jurisdiction in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: Neville surveys Foreign Relations records from 1900, 1903, 1906 and 1909 concerning leased Chinese ports, Russian and Japanese jurisdiction, and Dairen. He notes the Department’s approval of the view that U.S. consuls had no extraterritorial jurisdiction there. He finds no specific guidance on warship visits to leased territories.
